{"id": "9da2399c-3ce4-4f61-b52d-5774f12278fb", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "We're about to merge PR #14 in acme/payments-infra. It's the first infrastructure PR in that repo, there's no pipeline review set up, and finance wants to know what this stack is going to add to the AWS bill every month before we approve it. Can you work that out from the PR?

The attached material is what the repository integration and the AWS tools returned for this change. It is a synthetic test fixture: resource names, account results, SKUs and rates are made up, and the rates intentionally differ from real AWS list prices, so treat the rows below as the live lookup results for this run.

--- PR #14 (feature/ledger -> main) ---
Base branch main: no cloudformation/ directory.
Files added: cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml, .github/workflows/deploy.yml

--- .github/workflows/deploy.yml (excerpt) ---
env:
  AWS_REGION: eu-west-1
  STACK_NAME: payments-ledger
run: aws cloudformation deploy --stack-name payments-ledger --template-file cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml --region eu-west-1

--- cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml (Resources; Parameters hold only VPC and subnet IDs) ---
  LedgerDbSubnetGroup: {Type: AWS::RDS::DBSubnetGroup, Properties: {SubnetIds: [!Ref PrivateSubnetA, !Ref PrivateSubnetB]}}
  LedgerDb:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties: {Engine: postgres, DBInstanceClass: db.r6g.large, MultiAZ: true, AllocatedStorage: "200", StorageType: gp3, DBSubnetGroupName: !Ref LedgerDbSubnetGroup}
  ReconcilerNatEip: {Type: AWS::EC2::EIP, Properties: {Domain: vpc}}
  ReconcilerNatGateway: {Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway, Properties: {AllocationId: !GetAtt ReconcilerNatEip.AllocationId, SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetA}}
  AlbSecurityGroup: {Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup}
  ApiLoadBalancer:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties: {Type: application, Scheme: internet-facing, Subnets: [!Ref PublicSubnetA, !Ref PublicSubnetB], SecurityGroups: [!Ref AlbSecurityGroup]}
  ArchiveBucket: {Type: AWS::S3::Bucket, Properties: {VersioningConfiguration: {Status: Enabled}}}
  ReconcilerRole: {Type: AWS::IAM::Role}
  ReconcilerFunction: {Type: AWS::Lambda::Function, Properties: {Runtime: python3.12, Architectures: [arm64], MemorySize: 512, Role: !GetAtt ReconcilerRole.Arn}}

--- AWS (read-only), eu-west-1 ---
cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name payments-ledger
  -> ValidationError: Stack with id payments-ledger does not exist

--- pricing get-products (endpoint us-east-1, filter regionCode=eu-west-1), OnDemand terms only ---
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-01  usagetype EU-Multi-AZUsage:db.r6g.large   databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.500 USD per Hrs
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-09  usagetype EU-UnusedBox:db.r6g.large       databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.000 USD per Hrs   "unused capacity reservation hour"
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-02  usagetype EU-RDS:Multi-AZ-GP3-Storage     volumeType=General Purpose-GP3 databaseEngine=PostgreSQL   0.250 USD per GB-Mo
AmazonEC2  SKU FX-NAT-01  usagetype EU-NatGateway-Hours             productFamily=NAT Gateway   0.050 USD per Hrs
AmazonEC2  SKU FX-NAT-02  usagetype EU-NatGateway-Bytes             productFamily=NAT Gateway   0.050 USD per GB
AmazonVPC  SKU FX-IP-01   usagetype EU-PublicIPv4:InUseAddress                                  0.005 USD per Hrs
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-01  usagetype EU-LoadBalancerUsage            productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.025 USD per Hrs
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-03  usagetype EU-TS-LoadBalancerUsage         productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.006 USD per Hrs   "trust store unit-hour"
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-02  usagetype EU-LCUUsage                     productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.008 USD per LCU-Hrs", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "29cfd23d-5756-4451-846b-3c1719a0d646", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is a straightforward cost calculation I can compute directly from the fixture data without delegating or investigating further. I'll work through monthly costs using 730 hours/month as the standard AWS convention, starting with the LedgerDb RDS resource.

For RDS, the db.r6g.large Multi-AZ instance runs $0.500/hr × 730 hrs = $365/mo, plus 200GB of gp3 storage at $0.250/GB-Mo = $50/mo, giving $415/mo subtotal for RDS.

For the NAT Gateway and EIP, hourly NAT charges come to $36.50/mo, but data processing costs depend on traffic volume that isn't given, so I'll need to flag that as variable and assume an example volume. The EIP attached to the NAT gateway also has an in-use hourly rate in the fixture, so I should include that even though AWS often doesn't charge for EIPs attached to running resources in practice.

Security groups are free, so AlbSecurityGroup has no cost. For the ALB, I'm calculating LoadBalancerUsage at $0.025/hr × 730 = $18.25/mo, and excluding the trust store rate since mTLS isn't configured in this template.

LCU usage is traffic-dependent so I can't compute it without actual metrics, flagging it as variable. The ArchiveBucket has no S3 pricing rows in the fixture at all, so I need to flag that as a pricing gap, and the IAM role is free. Similarly, the Lambda function has no pricing data provided either - invocations and duration costs depend on actual usage, so that's another gap to note.

Summing the fixed, hours-based costs I can determine - RDS instance, RDS storage, NAT Gateway hourly, EIP, and ALB hourly - gives a subtotal of $473.40/mo, while NAT data processing, ALB LCU usage, trust store (inactive since mTLS isn't configured), and S3 storage remain unpriceable from the template alone.

I also don't have pricing data for Lambda invocation/duration, and the RDS unused capacity reservation SKU has a zero rate so it doesn't matter. I want to present a clear floor estimate while honestly flagging the usage-dependent costs and the two resources (S3, Lambda) where pricing data just wasn't available, then verify the math using standard 730 hours/month.

Adding up the fixed hourly-rate items - RDS Multi-AZ instance, RDS storage, NAT gateway, EIP, and ALB hours - I get a floor estimate of $473.40/month, excluding data transfer, LCU, S3 storage, and Lambda usage charges. This is a straightforward arithmetic task using the fixture data already provided, so no tool calls or investigation setup are needed.

I'll format the answer as a monthly cost table splitting fixed and variable components, and I'll be upfront about the pricing gaps for S3 and Lambda since that data wasn't given.

"}]}

{"id": "ded18cad-8f5a-45e1-81d6-c79cedbada9a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the monthly cost breakdown I can work out directly from PR #14's template, using the eu-west-1 rates returned for this run:

## Fixed, hourly-rate costs (calculable from the template alone)

Using a standard 730 hrs/month:

| Resource | Rate | Monthly |
|---|---|---|
| `LedgerDb` — db.r6g.large, Multi-AZ (instance-hours) | $0.500/hr | $365.00 |
| `LedgerDb` — 200 GB gp3 storage | $0.250/GB-Mo | $50.00 |
| `ReconcilerNatGateway` — hourly charge | $0.050/hr | $36.50 |
| `ReconcilerNatEip` — in-use public IPv4 | $0.005/hr | $3.65 |
| `ApiLoadBalancer` — ALB hourly charge | $0.025/hr | $18.25 |
| **Floor total** | | **$473.40/mo** |

(The RDS "unused capacity reservation" SKU is $0.000/hr, so it doesn't add anything.)

## Usage-dependent costs — can't be pinned down from the PR alone

These resources have per-GB or per-LCU rates that depend on traffic volume, which the template doesn't specify:
- **NAT Gateway data processing** — $0.050/GB (`ReconcilerNatGateway` will process all egress traffic from the reconciler's private subnet)
- **ALB LCU usage** — $0.008/LCU-Hr (depends on connections/throughput/rule evaluations)
- **ALB trust store** rate ($0.006/Hr) doesn't apply — no trust store/mTLS configured in this template

## Gaps — no pricing data returned for these resources

- **`ArchiveBucket`** (S3, versioning enabled) — no S3 pricing rows came back from the lookup, so I can't price storage or request costs for it.
- **`ReconcilerFunction`** (Lambda, arm64, 512MB) — no Lambda pricing rows came back either, so invocation/duration costs aren't covered.

**Bottom line for finance:** this stack has a predictable floor of **~$473/month** before any traffic touches it — dominated by the Multi-AZ RDS instance (**$365**, 77% of the floor). On top of that, actual NAT data transfer, ALB request/LCU volume, S3 storage, and Lambda usage will add more, but those need either a traffic estimate or a follow-up pricing lookup for S3/Lambda to quantify.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
